speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of your eyes and skin; this is a sign of jaundice. To determine the cause and severity, how many hours after birth did you notice the yellowing started, and is your baby feeding well?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since the jaundice appeared on day 14 and you are exclusively breastfeeding, could you tell me if your baby has passed any stool or urinated recently in the last 24 hours? Also, has anyone measured her bilirubin levels yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (likely physiological or insufficient intake due to exclusive breastfeeding, exacerbated by family history of metabolic liver disease). The onset at 2 weeks with exclusive breastfeeding and stable weight gain is most consistent with this condition, though the family history warrants monitoring for metabolic disorders.
